problem.title: Kashaev volume conjecture for hyperbolic knots

question.summary: Kashaev's quantum knot invariant is conjectured to grow at a rate fixed by the hyperbolic volume of the knot complement.
question.importance: The conjecture would let quantum knot invariants recover a geometric quantity of the knot complement. It links representation-theoretic data to three-dimensional hyperbolic geometry.
question.unresolved: Prove the volume-limit identity for every hyperbolic knot, or give a hyperbolic knot for which the limit fails or has the wrong value.

targetClauses.label: Universal volume-limit identity
targetClauses.text: For every hyperbolic knot, Kashaev's invariant has the stated volume asymptotic.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: Prove the identity for every hyperbolic knot, or exhibit a hyperbolic-knot counterexample.

claims.title: The universal hyperbolic-knot statement remains open
claims.text: TheoremDB's dated review found proofs for selected knots and families but no proof or counterexample for every hyperbolic knot.

claims.title: Colored Jones polynomials give an equivalent formulation
claims.text: Murakami and Murakami identify Kashaev's invariant with a root-of-unity specialization of the colored Jones polynomial and state the volume conjecture in that language.

decisions.rationale: Selected knots and families are known, but the universal statement has no accepted proof or counterexample.

provenance.label: Source-stated question
provenance.note: TheoremDB P3114 records Kashaev's universal hyperbolic-knot conjecture and cites the original papers.
